question.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of the Tangent Line to a Curve at a Point
question.problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $y=0.$ Given that the point $P(2,0,4)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}={e}^{y}+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡y$, find the equations of the tangent line to $C$ at $P.$
question.worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $y=0.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $P(2,0,4)$ will be given by the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(2,0)}.$

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂x}$ at $(2,0):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(2,0) & ={e}^{(0)}+2(2)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0) \\  & =1+4 \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-z{|}_{(2,0)} & =\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(2,0)}(x-2) \\ z-4 & =5(x-2) \\ z & =5x-6\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(2,0,4)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes, as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y=0 \\ z=5x-6\end{aligned}
$$

judgment.reasoning: All six answers are mathematically correct and supported by their own captured worked solutions. q-80473: g_xx=-4/(2x-y)² and g_yy=-1/(2x-y)², giving -5/9 at (1,-1). q-80468: both mixed partials equal 2xy sin(x²-y²), so their sum is 4xy sin(x²-y²). q-132590: fixing y=2 gives tangent slope f_x(-π/2,2)=-2; through the stated point, z=-2x+π. q-36372: fixing y=0 gives slope f_x(2,0)=5, hence z=5x-6. q-132604: fixing x=1 gives f_y(1,0)=-1 and tangent direction (0,1,-1); the selected vector (0,-1,1) is its negative and therefore equally valid. q-71221: fixing y=1 gives f_x(-1,1)=3 and tangent direction (1,0,3), explicitly stated in the source. No grade evidence was supplied; MA evidence comes from the worked solutions.
